input.title: Verify in production: the drain gate counts the run's own writes
input.body:
#1340's fix landed as 90dab0c (#1342): the scheduler run's drain gate now takes the union of what `listOpenWorkItems` returns with the issue numbers the run itself readied, instead of trusting the read alone.

It could not be watched at merge time. The unit tests prove `pickableCount`'s union logic, but the defect lived at the seam between the run's own writes and GitHub's eventually-consistent issue list — a seam no local test reaches. The fielded behaviour only becomes observable once a member's mount carries the new pack and its scheduler mints an item, which needs a converge cycle.

This matters more than most: the failure mode is a run that succeeds while silently dropping its own work. Nothing goes red, and it cost the fleet a full delivery cycle before anyone noticed.

Original-issue: #1340
In-production-when: `missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary`'s `.claudinite-settings.json` carries the `claudinite-tasks` pack entry at version `60824.5` or higher.
Verify: dispatch `claudinite-scheduler.yml` on that repo with input `wake: update`, then read the `scheduler-run` job's log. PASS if the run both logs a `- created #<n> ... (forced: ...)` (or `- woke #<n>`) line AND its next line reads `- N item(s) pickable — the drain job dispatches an executor`, and the run's `drain` job has a conclusion other than `skipped`. FAIL if the same run logs a create/wake and then `- nothing pickable`, or if `drain` is `skipped` despite a create/wake in that run.
Not-before: 2026-08-25T06:00:00Z
Retry-every: 1 day

Model: sonnet

### For the run executing this

1. Read `In-production-when:` against the real file on that repo's default branch. Never infer it from a merge, a green run, or elapsed time.
2. **Live** → run `Verify:`. Passes: comment the version you read and the two log lines you matched, then close this issue as completed. Fails: reopen #1340 with a comment saying what was asserted, what the log actually said and which run you read it from; comment here linking that; close this issue as completed.
3. **Not yet live** → push `Not-before:` forward by `Retry-every:`, clear this issue's `task:status:*` label, and leave it open. No comment; the bumped field is the record.

{"id":5235253537,"number":1340,"state":"closed","state_reason":"completed","locked":false,"title":"The drain gate reads the queue before its own writes are visible, so a forced wake mints work nothing drains","body":"`announcePickable` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/scheduler-run.mjs` takes the run's parting look by re-listing open issues over the REST API, immediately after the run's own writes. That read does not always see them, and when it doesn't, `pickable=false`, the drain job is skipped, and work the run just created waits for the next cron tick — up to twelve hours on the two-tick schedule.

## Seen live

ClaudiniteCanary, scheduler [run 32731101627](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/actions/runs/32731101627), dispatched with `wake: update`:

```
13:10:42.598  - created #253 claudinite-lifecycle/update (forced: it had no open standing item)
13:10:43.180  - nothing pickable — no executor is dispatched this run
```

584 ms apart. The `drain` job's `if: needs.scheduler-run.outputs.pickable == 'true'` evaluated false and the job shows `conclusion: skipped`. missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary#253 has sat `task:ready`, unclaimed, ever since — no executor run exists on that repo after 12:42.

The same repo's previous run, [32728430083](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteCanary/actions/runs/32728430083), got it right for a timing reason rather than a structural one:

```
12:41:58.162  - created #248 claudinite-lifecycle/update [task:ready]
12:41:58.738  - schedule board #148 updated (12 row(s))
12:42:05.578  - woke #236 claudinite-lifecycle/update
12:42:06.131  - 4 item(s) pickable — the drain job dispatches an executor
```

Eight seconds of other work sat between the creates and the read, and the read saw them. The failing run's only action was a single mint, so the gate read 584 ms after the write.

## Why it matters beyond one repo

This is a strong candidate for `fleet-baseline`'s recurring `did-not-converge` verdicts (#1330). The lever dispatches each member's scheduler with `wake: update`; on a member whose standing item has to be **minted** — exactly the "forced: it had no open standing item" case — the gate is at its most likely to miss, the drain skips, and the member converges nothing inside the follow window. A member that already had an open standing item has it in the list from the start and drains normally. The last two sweeps split 8/5 and 8/5.

The module's own header anticipated ordering (*"This is the run's LAST act, after the forced wake"*) but not read-after-write visibility.

## Fix direction

Don't wait, and don't re-read hoping. The run already knows what it created, readied and woke — union that set with what the list returns, and gate on the union. That removes the timing dependence entirely rather than widening a window. A sleep before the read would be the shape the corpus already rejects: a guard that names no condition.

Whatever the fix, prove it by driving a scheduler run whose *only* action is a single forced mint, and assert `pickable=true` — the passing shape above (several writes, seconds of other work) proves nothing about the failing one.

**#1342 is merged** as `90dab0c`. The fix is in `main`.

```
packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/   drain gate now unions the run's own writes
                                (created-as-ready / readied / reclaimed-to-ready /
                                woken) with the queue read; pickableCount exported
packs/claudinite-tasks/         version 60824.5 + VERSIONS.md row
```

Two things worth your attention from the merge:

**MissingBulbWebsite is genuinely fixed.** Its [13:44 run](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/actions/runs/32734426451) did 44 seconds of real work and its drain dispatched an executor — first success in ~470 runs. Worth noting it was never exposed to #1340: its workflow copy predates the gate, so its drain runs unconditionally.

**The earlier member re-dispatches never ran.** LaughCounter's was *cancelled* at 13:52 by the same 15-minute runner starvation that killed the first CI attempt — not skipped by the bug. So the fleet hasn't converged yet, and my earlier read of "queued behind contention" understated it: those runs died. I've re-dispatched all four now that runners are free.

I also filed **[#1343](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1343)** as a sub-issue of #1340 — the production check for the fix, since its real seam (a run's writes vs. GitHub's list read) is one no local test reaches. It waits on ClaudiniteCanary stamping `claudinite-tasks` at `60824.5`, then dispatches a forced wake and asserts the create and the `N item(s) pickable` line land in the same run with `drain` not skipped.

> ⏳ In flight:
> • **Four member schedulers re-dispatched** — LaughCounter, ShoutsAndWhispers, TLDR, ClaudiniteCanary. Checking in ~4 min; their `update` items are still `task:ready`.
> • **Runner starvation cancels jobs after 15 min queued** — it killed one CI attempt and all four earlier member dispatches. Worth knowing it presents as `cancelled`, not `failure`, so it reads as someone hitting stop.
>
> ⚠️ Still open:

* Repoint the queue workflows at the claudinite-tasks mount

The task surface moved out of the vendored engine into a pack, so every `run:`
line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
`.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already carries
the pack, and the canon keeps shims at the old paths until it retires them, so
both paths are live right now and this lands on its own.

Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs` — the same code that scaffolds these files — rather
than hand-edited, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should carry.
The cron is unchanged: it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it. The executor's secret
names are unchanged too, regenerated from this repo's own declarations.

`.github/workflows/` is the one directory a converge cannot write, which is why
this arrives as a pull request.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1331

* Drop the executor's comment about what not to put in it

Regenerated from the canon's stub after it lost the paragraph explaining why the
workflow does not serialise the whole secrets context. That is a note about an
edit rather than about the file in front of the reader, and it is pure freight
here: this file is vendored verbatim and nothing reads its comments. The reason
lives beside the code that stamps the secret list, in the pack's
converge-workflows.mjs.

input.title: The update precondition never asks whether the member is behind canon, so a stale member declines its own update
input.body:
`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/task.mjs` declines when the mount converged in the window and no declared pack moved:

```js
if (stamp.convergedInWindow && !(signals.sharedMount?.changedPacks ?? []).length) {
  return { run: false, reason: 'the mount converged in this window and no pack moved — nothing due' };
}
```

Both inputs are **purely local**, measured over the member's own window commits (`packs/claudinite-tasks/signals/index.mjs`):

- `stamp.convergedInWindow` — `commits.some((c) => c.files.some((f) => f.startsWith(\`${SHARED_SUBDIR}/\`)))`
- `sharedMount.changedPacks` — declared packs whose `.claudinite/shared/packs/<pack>/` files a window commit touched

Neither compares the member's stamp against the canon. `stamp` collects `canonHead`, and the precondition never reads it. So the question the task exists to answer — *am I behind?* — is never asked. What is asked is *did my mount move recently, and did that movement touch a declared pack?*

Those come apart exactly when the canon moves **after** a member's converge, inside the same window.

## Seen live

`missingbulb/LaughCounter` [#304](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/304), picked at 14:04:03 today and declined at 14:04:06 with `the mount converged in this window and no pack moved — nothing due`, closed `task:obsolete`.

Its `.claudinite-settings.json` at that moment, against canon `main`:

| Pack | LaughCounter | Canon |
|---|---|---|
| `basics` | 60823.1 | **60824.1** |
| `claudinite-growth` | 60823.2 | **60824.1** |
| `tidy-repo` | 60823.1 | **60824.1** |

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. ## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

{"number":1344,"title":"The update precondition never asks whether the member is behind canon, so a stale member declines its own update","body":"`packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/task.mjs` declines when the mount converged in the window and no declared pack moved:

```js
if (stamp.convergedInWindow && !(signals.sharedMount?.changedPacks ?? []).length) {
  return { run: false, reason: 'the mount converged in this window and no pack moved — nothing due' };
}
```

Both inputs are **purely local**, measured over the member's own window commits (`packs/claudinite-tasks/signals/index.mjs`):

- `stamp.convergedInWindow` — `commits.some((c) => c.files.some((f) => f.startsWith(\`${SHARED_SUBDIR}/\`)))`
- `sharedMount.changedPacks` — declared packs whose `.claudinite/shared/packs//` files a window commit touched

Neither compares the member's stamp against the canon. `stamp` collects `canonHead`, and the precondition never reads it. So the question the task exists to answer — *am I behind?* — is never asked. What is asked is *did my mount move recently, and did that movement touch a declared pack?*

Those come apart exactly when the canon moves **after** a member's converge, inside the same window.

## Seen live

`missingbulb/LaughCounter` [#304](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/issues/304), picked at 14:04:03 today and declined at 14:04:06 with `the mount converged in this window and no pack moved — nothing due`, closed `task:obsolete`.

Its `.claudinite-settings.json` at that moment, against canon `main`:

| Pack | LaughCounter | Canon |
|---|---|---|
| `basics` | 60823.1 | **60824.1** |
| `claudinite-growth` | 60823.2 | **60824.1** |
| `tidy-repo` | 60823.1 | **60824.1** |
| `claudinite-lifecycle` | 60823.1 | **60824.3** |
| `claudinite-tasks` | *absent* | **60824.5** (seeded by default) |

Four declared packs behind and one seeded pack missing entirely, and the task that maintains the mount concluded nothing was due. `missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers` and `missingbulb/TLDR` are in the same state, all three at `engineVersion 60823.1`.

## Why it matters

The decline is not self-correcting within the window, and **a forced wake cannot override it**: `wake:` readies the item, but the precondition is re-evaluated at pick, so the fleet lever mints work that converges to a no-op. That makes this a direct cause of `fleet-baseline`'s `did-not-converge` verdicts (#1330) — distinct from #1340, which was masking it. #1340 meant the item never got picked; with that fixed, the item now gets picked and declines.

It also inverts the intended reading of the reason string. "The mount converged and no pack moved" is meant to mean *we are current*. What it actually means is *nothing happened here lately* — which is equally true of a member that is current and one that is a day behind.

## Fix direction

Ask the real question. The stamp already carries `packVersions` and `engineVersion`, and `canonHead` is already collected — compare the member's stamped versions against the canon's declared ones and run when any differs, including a `seededByDefault` pack the member has no entry for. Local movement is then an optimisation on top of the comparison, not a substitute for it.

Note the corpus rule this sits against — *"Writing a task's precondition — gate on the objects' own movement in the window, never on standing state, which is true forever once true."* Being behind canon **is** standing state, and this is the case where that rule's converse bites: the object whose movement matters is the canon, and the member cannot see it move. The rule was written against a datetime that read stale forever (#1252); the correction overshot into never comparing at all.

Whatever the fix, prove it by driving a run on a member whose stamp is behind canon and whose mount converged inside the window — the LaughCounter shape above. A member that is current, or one that has not converged recently, does not exercise it.

Refs #1330, #1340

input.head: claudinite/declare-tasks-pack
input.body:
The task surface — the work-item queue, the executor, the task contract and the delivery lane — moved out of the vendored engine into its own `claudinite-tasks` pack (missingbulb/Claudinite#1317). This repo never got the declaration.

That is not cosmetic. The vendor set ships the pack's files whether or not they are declared, so the live workflows keep resolving — but `isActive` reads the literal `packs` list. Undeclared, the pack is **mounted and inert**: its tasks stop being discovered and the queue goes quiet with nothing red to say so.

The seed migration that should have written this (`2026-08-24-claudinite-tasks-seed`) cannot reach this repo, because the pack flow only runs migrations for packs the member already declares — a catch-22 tracked as missingbulb/Claudinite#1339.

## What changed

- `.claudinite-settings.json` — one added entry, `claudinite-tasks` at `60824.5`. Nothing else in the file is touched.
- `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/` — refreshed to that version, which carries the drain-gate fix from missingbulb/Claudinite#1340.

Generated by the canon's own `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` and the pack's `converge-workflows.mjs`, not by hand.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1339

input.head: claudinite/declare-tasks-pack
input.body:
The task surface — the work-item queue, the executor, the task contract and the delivery lane — moved out of the vendored engine into its own `claudinite-tasks` pack (missingbulb/Claudinite#1317). This repo never got the declaration.

That is not cosmetic. The vendor set ships the pack's files whether or not they are declared, so the live workflows keep resolving — but `isActive` reads the literal `packs` list. Undeclared, the pack is **mounted and inert**: its tasks stop being discovered and the queue goes quiet with nothing red to say so.

The seed migration that should have written this (`2026-08-24-claudinite-tasks-seed`) cannot reach this repo, because the pack flow only runs migrations for packs the member already declares — a catch-22 tracked as missingbulb/Claudinite#1339.

## What changed

- `.claudinite-settings.json` — one added entry, `claudinite-tasks` at `60824.5`. Nothing else in the file is touched.
- `.github/workflows/claudinite-scheduler.yml` and `claudinite-executor.yml` — regenerated from the pack's own stubs, so their `run:` lines name the pack mount rather than the retiring engine paths. `.github/workflows/` is the one directory a converge cannot write, which is why this arrives as a pull request.

The cron is unchanged: it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own `taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it. The executor's secret names are regenerated from this repo's own declarations.

Generated by the canon's own `vendoring/apply-vendor-set.mjs` and the pack's `converge-workflows.mjs`, not by hand.

Refs missingbulb/Claudinite#1339

# /do-later — defer a change into a chained request run

The owner has spotted a change that should happen **after** the work in front of
them. Doing it now derails the session; an ordinary issue waits for somebody to
remember it. This files it as an **ad-hoc request** (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §16):
an issue the queue picks up on its own, held behind what is still in flight.

You are filing work, not doing it. Touch no source file, open no branch.

## What you write

**One issue, well defined.** The run that implements it will never see this
conversation — the issue body is the whole brief. State the change, the files or
surfaces it touches if you know them, what "done" looks like, and anything the
owner ruled out. Size it to its idea; a rename is a sentence.

Give the body these two lines, verbatim in this spelling — the scheduler run reads the
first one:

```
Blocked-by: #<what this waits on>

<!-- filed by /do-later -->
```

**What it waits on**, first match wins:

1. the issue of the **previous `/do-later` you filed in this session** — that is
   the chain the owner asked for, each deferral behind the last;
2. otherwise the **pull request** the session's work is on, if one is open;
3. otherwise the **issue** the session is working on;
4. otherwise nothing — omit the field, and say in your reply that it queues
   immediately.

Only ever name blockers that will actually *close* — a merged PR does, a branch
does not. If you filed an earlier `/do-later` this session but no longer have its
number, find it by its marker line among the repo's open issues rather than
falling back to (2).

## The mark, and the parameters in the body

**The mark is one label**: **`task:origin:ad-hoc`** (`mcp__github__issue_write`,
`labels`). The next scheduler run adopts the issue — writing its machine block
into the body and giving it a status — and the issue itself becomes the work
item, so the whole run plays out where the owner is already looking. Nothing else
is a label any more; everything below rides the issue **body**, and is honoured
only for an author with push access on the repository.

- **`Model: <family>`** — the family **this** session is running, so the deferred
  work is done by what the owner is working with now. Read it with `get_session`
  (claude-code-remote, `session_id` omitted) and map `session_context.model` to
  `opus`, `sonnet` or `haiku`. A model outside those three is left out, and the
  run takes the task's default.
- **`Automerge: if-narrow`** — the standing authorization to land the change
  without the owner's approval **when the run's diff turns out to be narrow**
  (docs, tests, comment-only edits, and code within a single directory; the run
  measures this, not you). **Withhold it whenever the owner said they want to see
  this one** — "let me review it", "show me before merging", or any such wording
  outranks how small the change looks.
- **`Task: <pack>/<task>`** — only when the deferral is a run of a *named task*
  rather than "implement this issue". Left out, the run is the built-in request
  implementer, which is what a `/do-later` almost always wants.

Keep the fields on their own lines, above the marker line, beside `Blocked-by:`.

If the mark does not exist in the repository yet, it cannot be applied (the API
refuses an unknown label, and only the scheduler run creates it). Say so in your
reply and leave the issue filed — the label appears on the next scheduler run, and
the owner can mark it from the issue page.

## Then say what you filed

One line back to the owner: the issue link, what it waits on, the model family,
and whether it will merge itself or come back for approval.

{"number":1317,"title":"Extract the task execution/scheduling surface into a claudinite-tasks pack","body":"Tracking issue for the split of `engine/scheduler/` (52% of core, 8,106 lines) out of the engine and into a canon pack, so the engine is pack distribution only. End state and rationale: `docs/tasks-dispatch/DESIGN.md` **§18** (folded into the mechanism's own design doc — no standalone document).

## Agreed end state (summary — DESIGN.md §18 is authoritative)

- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` owns the whole task surface: queue, executor, signals, task contract, calendar/anchor math, dispatch, run-records, code-work, delivery helpers (`land-pr`, `deliver-generated`), GitHub REST helpers, the two workflow stubs, the operational `.md`s, and the `implement-request` built-in as an ordinary pack task.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*` is the pack's published import surface — the one sanctioned cross-pack import in the corpus (barriers-enforced). Consumers: claudinite-dashboard (title grammar, outcome decode, anchor math) and every pack task that delivers (delivery + gh helpers).
- Queue meta-machinery relocates in: `task-janitor` (from basics), `usage-fold` (from claudinite-growth), the task-declaration checks (from claudinite-growth worldRules) — and the simulator + scenario suite (`docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/`), the mechanism's executable spec, into the pack's own `test/`.
- The update flows (`updates/*`) move into `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/`; old `updates/*` paths stay as callable shims until no fielded vendored worker names them.
- `converge-wiring` splits: distribution wiring (hooks, rules index, gitattributes, badges) stays engine; workflow/scheduling wiring moves to the pack. Bootstrap stops wiring task machinery; adopting `claudinite-tasks` scaffolds it.

input.title: Move taskScheduler from a top-level settings key into the claudinite-tasks pack's own config
input.body:
`.claudinite-settings.json` carries `taskScheduler` as a **top-level key**, beside `packs`, `accept` and `sharedConstants`:

```json
"taskScheduler": {
  "agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints": { "default": { "url": "…", "tokenSecret": "CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN" } },
  "dailyHour": 4,
  "weeklyDay": "Sun",
  "monthlyDay": 1
}
```

Every one of those settings belongs to `claudinite-tasks`. Now that the task surface is a pack (#1317) and every member declares it, this is settings for a pack sitting outside that pack's declaration — where every other pack's settings live in its own `config` block (`barriers` rules, `claude-code-web-users-support` store, `claudinite-dashboard` mode, `node` dirs). A repo that does not declare `claudinite-tasks` can still carry a `taskScheduler` block that nothing reads.

Target shape:

```json
{ "id": "claudinite-tasks", "config": { "dailyHour": 4, "weeklyDay": "Sun", "monthlyDay": 1, "agenticTaskInvocationEndpoints": { … } } }
```

## What it touches

`taskScheduler` is read at **46 sites across 17 modules**. The ones that matter:

- `engine/checks/helpers/repo-context.mjs` — `loadConfig`, plus `ENDPOINTS_KEY` / `LEGACY_ENDPOINTS_KEY`; the natural place for a single resolver every other caller goes through.
- `packs/claudinite-tasks/` — `converge-workflows.mjs`, `hash-minute.mjs`, `calendar`/anchors, `queue/scheduler-run.mjs`, `queue/executor.mjs`, `queue/invoke.mjs`, `task-contract.mjs`, `signals/fleet.mjs`, `worldRules/task-declaration-shape.mjs`, `tasks/task-janitor/queue-sweep.mjs`.
- `packs/claudinite-dashboard/` — `view-repo.mjs`, `fleet.mjs` (cross-pack readers of the same block).
- `engine/scheduler/converge-wiring.mjs` — retiring with the shims, check whether it still needs touching when this runs.
- `vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs` — fixtures spell the shape and will need both forms while the tolerance stands.

## Done looks like

- One resolver owns the lookup; no module reaches into either shape directly.
- The reader **accepts the legacy top-level key at the door** and keeps doing so — this is the accept-legacy-input rule, so nothing waits on stragglers. A member on the old shape keeps working indefinitely.
- A migration record moves the block into the pack entry for every member that declares `claudinite-tasks`, preserving the values exactly (`dailyHour` in particular, since the hashed cron is derived from it and a changed value silently reschedules the repo).
- The tolerance's removal is gated on **no member still stamping the top-level key**, read off the stamps — never a date. That is a separate change, not this one.
- `.claudinite-settings.json`'s schema (whatever `$schema` points at) reflects the new shape.

## Watch for

- **`dailyHour` is load-bearing.** `hashedCron` takes the repo's full name *and* `dailyHour`; if the migration drops or defaults it, the repo's cron minute and anchor hours move and its queue quietly reschedules. Assert the regenerated cron is byte-identical before and after on a real member's settings.
- **The endpoint token name is a secret name, not a secret.** It rides into the executor workflow's env via `declaredSecrets`; moving the block must not change the generated secret list, or every member needs a workflow PR.
- **`claudinite-dashboard` reads it cross-pack.** It has no dependency on `claudinite-tasks` and must not gain one — the resolver's home needs to be somewhere both can reach, which is the engine helper, not the pack.

Blocked-by: #1317

Model: opus
Automerge: if-narrow

<!-- filed by /do-later -->

The task surface moved out of the vendored engine into its own pack (#1317).

The declaration was never written for this repo. The vendor set ships the pack's
files whether or not they are declared, so the live workflows keep resolving —
but `isActive` reads the literal list, so undeclared the pack is mounted and
inert: its tasks stop being discovered and the queue goes quiet with nothing red
to say so.

Both workflow files are regenerated from the pack's own stubs, so their `run:`
lines name the pack mount rather than the retiring engine paths. The cron is
unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own dailyHour, so
regenerating reproduces it — and the executor's secret names are regenerated
from this repo's own declarations.

Generated by the canon's own vendoring and workflow converge, not by hand.

Filed: **[#1346](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1346)** — move `taskScheduler` out of the top level and into the `claudinite-tasks` pack's own `config`, waiting on **[#1317](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1317)** (the migration tracker — no open PR left from this session, so that's the chain anchor), running on **opus**, marked `Automerge: if-narrow`. In practice it'll come back for your approval: it touches 46 read sites across 17 modules plus a migration record, which the run won't measure as narrow.

I put three things in the brief that the implementing run won't otherwise know:

- **`dailyHour` is load-bearing** — `hashedCron` derives the cron minute *and* anchor hours from it, so a migration that defaults or drops it silently reschedules the repo's queue. Assert the regenerated cron is byte-identical on a real member.
- **The endpoint `tokenSecret` is a secret *name*** that rides into the executor workflow's env via `declaredSecrets` — if the move changes the generated list, every member needs a workflow PR.
- **`claudinite-dashboard` reads the block cross-pack** and must not gain a dependency on `claudinite-tasks`, so the resolver belongs in the engine helper rather than the pack.

Separately, the verification I left running came back: **LaughCounter's scheduler ran green at 19:01 on the merge commit `ec2f525`** — its queue now executes from `packs/claudinite-tasks/queue/` and the whole thing works end to end.

> ✅ Done:
> • **[#1346](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1346)** filed, blocked behind [#1317](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1317), `task:origin:ad-hoc` applied — the next scheduler run adopts it.
> • **LaughCounter verified green** from the pack path on the merged head.
>
> ⚠️ Still open:
> • **[#1344](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1344)** — the precondition still never compares against canon. Today's sweep cured 12 repos; the cause is untouched and can strand them again.
> • **[#1339](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1339)** — now moot, wants closing with a note.
> • **[#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329)** — L4 unblocked, base stale at `a248483`, needs a rebase.
> • **TLDR and MissingBulbWebsite verification runs** — dispatched, not yet read.

{"total_count":41,"workflow_runs":[{"id":32765715397,"name":"Claudinite scheduler","display_title":"Claudinite scheduler","workflow_id":320961748,"run_number":500,"run_attempt":1,"event":"workflow_dispatch","status":"completed","conclusion":"success","head_branch":"main","head_sha":"055d7f45d866511aafe4c3b47c0905c28020bc5e","head_commit":{"message":"Converge the mount onto the current canon and declare claudinite-tasks (#371)

The task surface moved out of the vendored engine into its own pack (#1317).

The declaration was never written for this repo. The vendor set ships the pack's
files whether or not they are declared, so the live workflows keep resolving —
but `isActive` reads the literal list, so undeclared the pack is mounted and
inert: its tasks stop being discovered and the queue goes quiet with nothing red
to say so.

Both workflow files are regenerated from the pack's own stubs, so their `run:`
lines name the pack mount rather than the retiring engine paths. The cron is
unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own dailyHour, so
regenerating reproduces it — and the executor's secret names are regenerated
from this repo's own declarations.

Generated by the canon's own vendoring and workflow converge, not by hand.

Refs #271.

Lands two keepers from the conversation half — both confirmed independently
across the fresh logs since the last landed run (dispatch #248, 08-13): two
sessions on this repo's own procedures paid for the same friction twice, and
one MCP-tool claim from a third log was checked directly against the live
tool before landing (it didn't hold).

- npm run test:all chains four sub-suites (root, server, extension,
  dev/requirements); piping its output through `tail -N` drops the real exit
  code (becomes tail's own) and truncates earlier suites' pass/fail
  summaries, forcing a second full ~13-15s run to see what the first one's
  own output already contained (hit on #253 and #264).
- mcp__github__actions_list list_workflow_runs ignores per_page for this
  repo's busiest workflows — verified directly: per_page:3 against
  chrome-extension-release.yml (93 runs) still returned the tool's default
  page of 30, ~410KB, blowing the MCP token cap on the first call every
  time (hit on #251 and #262). Go straight to the tool's saved overflow
  file instead of retrying with a smaller page.

Not landed: #251's read of that same log also flagged a filename resource_id
returning total_count:0 as a trap. Re-tested directly (both by filename and
by numeric id) — it's not a bug, chrome-extension-daily-release.yml is a
workflow_call-only reusable workflow with no runs of its own, so 0 is
correct. Noted inline instead of landed as a lesson.

The activity half (commit fc73d64/#279, PR #285, issues #282/#280) was all
Claudinite engine/vendoring plumbing — explicitly out of scope for this
pack's local capture.

Writes confined to .claudinite/local/packs/tldr/RULES.md.

The task surface moved out of the vendored engine into its own pack (#1317).

The declaration was never written for this repo. The vendor set ships the pack's
files whether or not they are declared, so the live workflows keep resolving —
but `isActive` reads the literal list, so undeclared the pack is mounted and
inert: its tasks stop being discovered and the queue goes quiet with nothing red
to say so.

Both workflow files are regenerated from the pack's own stubs, so their `run:`
lines name the pack mount rather than the retiring engine paths. The cron is
unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own dailyHour, so
regenerating reproduces it — and the executor's secret names are regenerated
from this repo's own declarations.

Generated by the canon's own vendoring and workflow converge, not by hand.

Closes #242

The tldr pack's "three version records" section existed to work around a drift
the pipeline created: the daily auto-release patch-bumps only the two paths
named in .github/release.config, so the repo-root package.json fell behind after
every release and cer/version-sync re-filed it BLOCKING as "expected drift".

Removes the drift instead of documenting it: the extension version is declared
as a sharedConstants entry (regex mode) across extension/manifest.json,
extension/package.json and the root package.json, and the daily release aligns
the root file inside the bump commit. The RULES.md section is deleted whole,

{"number":1329,"title":"Delete the legacy shims left by the claudinite-tasks extraction","body":"PR D of #1317 — the gated tail. Written now so the stack takes one approval, **merged only at chain link L4**.

Closes #1328

> ⚠️ **Do not merge yet.** L1 must show every member's stamp carrying the pack, L2 must repoint each member's workflow `run:` lines and routine prompts, and L3 must observe a full queue cycle running from the new paths. Merging before that leaves members whose live workflows name files this PR deletes, with nothing able to repair them.

Based on `claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq` (#1326), so the diff shows only the deletion.

## What goes

- `engine/scheduler/*` and `updates/*` — both shim trees, each with its `legacy-entry.mjs`.
- The reviewed barrier exception that let `engine/scheduler/` name a pack.
- The vendor set's two temporary rules: the engine walk that shipped the shims only where the pack shipped, and the tolerance that shipped `claudinite-tasks` whether or not a member declared it. Past L3 the declaration decides, with nothing added to it.

## Two tests carry the confirmation

The point of the chain is that the retirement is *observed*, not assumed, so the tests say which:

- `engine-pack-lane-shims` gains a `RETIRED` list holding `engine/scheduler/*`. The condition for putting a path there is written at the definition: its fielded callers were read and found gone — never "the current tree does not import it", which is the one thing the scan exists because you cannot rely on.
- The fielded-flow surface in `install.test.mjs` names the flows at `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/`, which is the same fact from the other side: a worker one cycle behind loads them from the canon tree it just fetched.

Two canon call sites that had been going through the `updates/` shim now name the real path; one dangling link in the canary pack's README is repointed.

## Verification

Full suite 0 failures; `check_the_work` clean; `check_the_world` 0 blocking. The advisory count drops from 142 to 84 — the difference is the `file-placement` advisories the shim files were carrying.

## Folders touched

```
engine/scheduler/         deleted
updates/                  deleted
vendoring/                the shim gating and the undeclared-pack tolerance come out
.claudinite-settings.json the engine/scheduler barrier exception comes out
```

input.body:
**Not merged. As written this wedges every member on its next update run.**

L4's stated preconditions are now met — all 13 members stamp `claudinite-tasks 60824.5`, and every member's workflow `run:` lines name the pack mount. I went to merge this and found a separate blocker the chain doesn't cover.

## The defect

This PR deletes `updates/`. The update worker still calls:

```js
const { engineUpdate } = await load('updates/engine-update.mjs');
const { packUpdate }   = await load('updates/pack-update.mjs');
const { terminalFor }  = await load('updates/terminals.mjs');
```

Both on `main` (`90dab0c`) and on this branch (`77d73c8`) — the PR does not repoint them, despite the body claiming "two canon call sites that had been going through the `updates/` shim now name the real path".

`load` resolves against a **fresh canon clone at HEAD**, not the member's mount:

```js
git(['clone', '--depth', '1', CANON_URL, tmp]);
const load = async (rel) => import(pathToFileURL(join(tmp, rel)).href);
```

So the surface a member calls is whatever *its* vendored worker names, resolved against *today's* canon. Every member vendored a worker naming `updates/*` earlier today. Delete `updates/` and the next update run on all 13 fails at module resolution — and cannot self-repair, because the repair is the update.

This is the case `basics/RULES.md` already names: *"Changing an export in `updates/*` — empty it, never remove it… Fielded workers are stale callers of instantly-current flow modules, so a removal wedges every member permanently on its next run."*

The `install.test.mjs` change actively hides it: it rewrites the fielded-flow surface to name only the pack paths, so the one test guarding this stops asserting the surface members actually call.

## What is safe, and what the split looks like

The two shim trees have different retirement conditions and cannot go in one step.

**`engine/scheduler/*` — safe now.** Nothing in the canon imports it (only tests reference it), and it is named by member *workflow files*, which all now point at the pack. Verified across all 13.

**`updates/*` — needs one more converge cycle.** Its retirement gate is "no member's vendored worker names it", which requires first landing a worker that names `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/*`, then letting the fleet converge, then reading the members.

I built and tested the safe half locally — delete `engine/scheduler/`, repoint the worker's three `load()` calls, keep `updates/`, and pin **both** surfaces in `install.test.mjs` — and it is green: full suite 2734 passing, `check_the_world` 0 blocking.

I did not push it, for one reason: deleting `engine/scheduler/` makes 21 deliberately-legacy references dangle, and `check_the_work` blocks on all of them. They are not stale pointers. Ten are in `vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`, which models a member's *pre-existing* workflow (naming `tick.mjs`, older still) precisely so the rehearsal proves the converge migrates it; the rest are historical wire-protocol strings like `'Execute the Claudinite executor: engine/scheduler/executor.md'`, which the decoder must handle forever. Clearing them needs judgement per site — waiver with a reason, or teaching `reference-integrity` about legacy fixture text — and that is a change of its own, not something to rush behind a merge at the end of a long session.

## Recommended shape

1. **Now:** delete `engine/scheduler/*`, repoint the worker, keep `updates/*`, pin both surfaces, and resolve the 21 legacy references deliberately. Retires the vendor-set engine-walk rule and the undeclared-pack tolerance, both of which are safe today.
2. **After one converge cycle**, gated on reading members' vendored workers — not a date: delete `updates/*`.

Leaving this PR open and unmerged; its diff is the starting point for step 1 minus the `updates/` deletion.

Closing — resolved by removing the condition rather than fixing the mechanism.

This was a catch-22: the seed record `2026-08-24-claudinite-tasks-seed` declares `claudinite-tasks` into every member running scheduled work, but the pack flow only runs migrations for packs a member **already declares**, so the record could never reach a member that lacked the declaration. `seedDeclaration` is no help either — it writes only when the settings file is absent, i.e. fresh repos only.

All 13 members now declare the pack, converged from the canon side today:

| | |
|---|---|
| CrosswordChat | [#316](https://github.com/missingbulb/CrosswordChat/pull/316) |
| ShoutsAndWhispers | [#286](https://github.com/missingbulb/ShoutsAndWhispers/pull/286) |
| MissingBulbWebsite | [#230](https://github.com/missingbulb/MissingBulbWebsite/pull/230) |
| ClaudiniteWebsite | [#299](https://github.com/missingbulb/ClaudiniteWebsite/pull/299) |
| EdFringeNow | [#498](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/498) |
| VascularColoring | [#268](https://github.com/missingbulb/VascularColoring/pull/268) |
| GoogleCalendarEventCreator | [#1057](https://github.com/missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator/pull/1057) |
| hitbut | [#119](https://github.com/missingbulb/hitbut/pull/119) |
| WIP | [#98](https://github.com/missingbulb/WIP/pull/98) |
| Shepherd | [#264](https://github.com/missingbulb/Shepherd/pull/264) |
| LaughCounter | [#305](https://github.com/missingbulb/LaughCounter/pull/305) |
| TLDR | [#371](https://github.com/missingbulb/TLDR/pull/371) |

ClaudiniteCanary already declared it. Every stamp reads `claudinite-tasks 60824.5`.

The seed record has nothing left to apply to, so the underlying catch-22 is no longer reachable **for this pack**. It is not fixed in general: the next `seededByDefault` pack introduced to an existing fleet will hit exactly the same wall, and the fix — having the pack flow consider seeded-but-undeclared packs, or giving the record a path that does not depend on the declaration it is trying to write — remains unwritten. Worth its own issue when that next pack appears rather than carrying this one open against a condition that no longer exists.

content.text:
Fleet force is running; I'll read it when it lands. Here's where everything stands.

## L4 / #1329 — stopped, deliberately

I did not merge it, despite your LGTM, because **it would wedge all 13 members on their next update run.** The evidence, verified on both `main` and the branch:

```js
// packs/claudinite-lifecycle/tasks/update/worker.mjs:162
const { engineUpdate } = await load('updates/engine-update.mjs');
```

`load` resolves against a **fresh canon clone at HEAD**, not the member's mount. The PR deletes `updates/` without repointing those calls — so every member's next update fails at module resolution, and can't self-repair because the repair *is* the update. Its body claims the call sites were repointed; they weren't. Worse, its `install.test.mjs` change rewrites the fielded-flow surface to name only the new paths, which switches off the one test guarding this.

This is the failure `basics/RULES.md` already names: *empty an `updates/*` export, never remove it.*

The two shim trees have different retirement gates and can't go together:
- **`engine/scheduler/*`** — safe now; nothing imports it and all 13 workflows name pack paths.
- **`updates/*`** — needs one converge cycle first, so members field a worker naming `packs/claudinite-lifecycle/updates/*`.

I built and tested the safe half (full suite 2734 green, `check_the_world` 0 blocking) but didn't push it: deleting `engine/scheduler/` makes 21 *deliberately-legacy* references dangle — ten in `vendoring/rehearsal/fixtures.mjs`, which models a pre-migration member on purpose, and the rest historical wire-protocol strings the decoder must keep handling. Clearing those needs per-site judgement, not a rushed sweep behind a merge. Full analysis is on [#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329#issuecomment-5400062897).

## Closed

- **[#1339](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1339)** — resolved by removing the condition: all 13 declare the pack, so the catch-22 has nothing to bite. I noted that it's *not* fixed generally — the next `seededByDefault` pack added to an existing fleet hits the same wall.
- **[#1327](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1327)** — superseded; its commits landed via #1326's squash, which is why GitHub couldn't detect it.

## Fleet

All 13 members at `claudinite-tasks 60824.5` on converged mounts. `fleet-baseline` forced via Shepherd. Worth flagging: with [#1344](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1344) unfixed, a forced update *declines* on a member whose mount already converged — so expect this sweep to report no-ops rather than work, which is correct here since I converged everything by hand.

> ⚠️ Still open:
> • **[#1344](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/issues/1344)** — the precondition never compares against canon. Unfixed, and the reason a fleet force can't do what it looks like it does.
> • **[#1329](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1329)** — left open with the split documented; needs the two-step reshape, not a merge.
> • **11 other canon PRs** — growth/promotion work (#1345, #1303, #1299, #1285, #1284, #1283, #1204, #1157, #1152, #1031, #1021) plus **[#1234](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1234)**, which still says DO NOT MERGE YET on its face.
> • **Fleet force in flight** — reading it shortly.

* Republish the dashboard when the mount moves, not only on a human push

The published site is stuck on claudinite-dashboard v10 while main's mount
carries v12, so the fleet grid still shows the "mount has not converged in
N days" verdict v11 removed. Nothing is wrong with the page: the deploy
never fires. Claudinite's update PRs are auto-merged by github-actions[bot],
and a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no workflow, so every converge
lands without a build.

The catch-up follows the vendored scheduler, which is this repo's one
permitted cron, and asks on each of its wake-ups whether the page's sources
have moved since the last successful deploy — so the hourly cadence costs a
cache lookup rather than an hourly republish of identical bytes.

* Hash every generated artifact, not the roster by name

The already-deployed gate hashed `usage-fleet.GENERATED.json` because that
is what this deployment's roster happens to be called — but the roster's
file name is per-deployment config, and a member list that changed under a
different name would leave the site serving the old one. The glob is
over-inclusive by design: an extra rebuild costs one run, a missed one
costs a stale page.

Keeps this file identical to the pack's stub below its header.

Regenerated from the canon's stubs by the tasks pack's own
`converge-workflows.mjs`, so this is exactly what the pack says this repo should
be carrying — not a hand-edit of five lines.

Two changes arrive together because they live in the same two files, and
`.github/workflows/` moves only through a human-merged PR:

- Every `run:` line moves from `.claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/…` to
  `.claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-tasks/…`. This repo's mount already
  carries the pack, and the legacy shims stay until the canon's L4, so the two
  paths are live at once and this can land on its own.
- The executor's `CLAUDINITE_SECRETS: ${{ toJSON(secrets) }}` becomes the two
  secrets this repo's tasks actually declare. Serialising the whole secrets
  context is the shape GitHub's malicious-workflow detection flags: this repo's
  executor runs have been parking with zero jobs, waiting on a human click that
  an unattended queue can neither absorb nor notice.

The cron is unchanged — it is hashed from the repo's full name and its own
`taskScheduler.dailyHour`, so regenerating reproduces it.

* Republish the dashboard when the mount moves, not only on a human push

The published site is stuck on claudinite-dashboard v10 while main's mount
carries v12, so the fleet grid still shows the "mount has not converged in
N days" verdict v11 removed. Nothing is wrong with the page: the deploy
never fires. Claudinite's update PRs are auto-merged by github-actions[bot],
and a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN triggers no workflow, so every converge
lands without a build.

The catch-up follows the vendored scheduler, which is this repo's one
permitted cron, and asks on each of its wake-ups whether the page's sources
have moved since the last successful deploy — so the hourly cadence costs a
cache lookup rather than an hourly republish of identical bytes.

is what this deployment's roster happens to be called — but the roster's
file name is per-deployment config, and a member list that changed under a
different name would leave the site serving the old one. The glob is
over-inclusive by design: an extra rebuild costs one run, a missed one
costs a stale page.

Keeps this file identical to the pack's stub below its header.

{"number":1234,"title":"DO NOT MERGE YET — retire the twice-daily-cron migration tolerances","body":"**This PR is written for review now and merged later.** Phase D of #1225 — the destructive tail. `writing-migration-plans`: all the code including the tail is written and approved in one pass so the owner's attention is spent once; what waits is the *merge*, and what performs it is a link in the chain rather than anyone's memory.

Stacked on #1230 (phases B and C). Base moves to `main` once that lands.

## What it removes, and what gates each

**The frequency tolerance.** `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` is **emptied, not deleted** — the map *is* the tolerance, so emptying it collapses `ACCEPTED_FREQUENCIES` onto `FREQUENCIES`, makes a declaration still naming a retired token fail contract validation, and leaves `normalizeFrequency` as the identity every caller can keep calling. Nothing has to be unwired, and a later retirement fills the map in again.

> *Gate:* no member's own task declarations still name a retired token. Converge-confirmable, never a date. Emptying early doesn't merely fail such a task — it makes `periodMs` judge it against a bound it was never sized for, which is the two-hour staleness park the whole door exists to prevent.

**The cron tolerance.** `scheduler-workflow-shape` stops accepting the hourly line.

> *Gate:* every member's workflow PR has landed. This is **earlier** than the other gate, so if it arrives well ahead, split the commit and merge this half alone.

## Reviewer note — the stacked-PR false green

`check_the_work` passed before I'd bumped anything, because the diff against `main` already carries #1230's own `claudinite-lifecycle` bump and the check read it as this PR's (#1119). Bumped to `60822.3` explicitly. **This needs re-verifying after #1230 merges and this branch rebases** — the false green survives right up until then.

Suite 2606/2606, `check_the_work` and `check_the_world` both 0 blocking.

Closes #1233

input.title: Stop the update precondition guessing whether the member is behind
input.head: claude/pack-migration-tasks-9hw4tq
input.body:
The question this task exists to ask — *is this member behind the canon?* — **cannot be asked from a scheduler run.** The Action deliberately does not read canon (DESIGN §3.3): `stamp.canonHead` is always null, and no signal carries the canon's versions.

That correction matters, because #1344's own "fix direction" said to compare the stamp against the canon's declared versions. It isn't implementable without reversing that design decision and putting a canon fetch in every member's hourly scheduler run. This PR takes the other route.

## What was wrong

Two proxies have stood in for the unavailable comparison, and both answered a different question:

- A **datetime in the declaration** recorded the last *full re-vendor*, so a member converging nightly read as months overdue forever (#1252).
- **Local movement in the window** — `convergedInWindow && !changedPacks.length` — reads as *"nothing happened here lately"*, which is equally true of a member that is current and one that canon moved past an hour after its own converge.

The second proxy is what stalled the fleet today. LaughCounter and TLDR sat four declared packs behind and missing a seeded one, each declining its own update at pick:

```
14:04:03  Claimed by executor actions-32736360596
14:04:06  The precondition declined: the mount converged in this window and no pack moved — nothing due
```

A forced wake could not override it — `wake:` readies the item, but the precondition is re-evaluated at pick, so the fleet lever mints work that converges to a no-op. Both members had to be converged from the canon side by hand.

## The change

The decline is gone. Only `!stamp.present` remains — a repo with no mount has nothing to update.

The asymmetry settles it, and it is not close: **declining wrongly costs permanent, silent staleness that nothing in the member can repair; running wrongly costs one converge that finds nothing and exits.** The precondition's own contract already says it "gates only that the worker RUNS; the worker owns every decision after that" — this stops it second-guessing the worker on a question it cannot see the inputs to.

Cost is one no-op converge per member per day, since the task is `frequency: 'daily'`.

## Verification

The test that asserted the decline now asserts the opposite, written first and watched fail. Full suite 2734 passing, `check_the_work` clean.

Closes #1344

input.title: create-extractor declares a retired frequency token, and it is the last thing holding a canon migration open
input.body:
`.claudinite/local/packs/gcec/tasks/create-extractor/task.mjs:23`:

```js
frequency: 'hourly',           // a submitted request should become a PR in minutes, not overnight
```

`hourly` is a **retired** frequency token. It still loads only because the canon carries a tolerance — `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES` in `packs/claudinite-tasks/calendar.mjs`, which normalizes `hourly → daily` at the declaration door.

Two consequences, and the comment above shows they pull against each other:

1. **This task is already not hourly.** `normalizeFrequency` maps it to `daily` before anything downstream sees it — the anchor, the janitor's stale-ready bound, and the precondition's signal window all read `daily`. So the latency the comment asks for ("minutes, not overnight") is not what the task currently gets, and hasn't been since the token was retired.
2. **It is the last blocker on a canon migration.** missingbulb/Claudinite#1234 retires the tolerance by emptying `LEGACY_FREQUENCIES`. Once that lands, this declaration fails contract validation and the task stops loading entirely. A fleet-wide check of every member's local task declarations found this is the only remaining occurrence.

## The decision

Not a mechanical rename — the retirement's own mapping is `hourly → daily`, which is precisely the behaviour the comment exists to avoid. Roughly:

- **Accept `daily`** if overnight turnaround is in fact acceptable, and drop the comment's claim. Cheapest, and matches what the task already does today.
- **Trigger on the event instead of a cron.** A submitted request is an issue/label event; the queue's executor already fires on `issues: labeled`. A task with `frequency: 'manual'` woken by whatever knows the request arrived gives minutes-level latency without a cron, and is what the canon recommends for work with no natural cadence.
- **Argue for keeping an hourly cadence** as a supported token, which is a canon-side change to the frequency vocabulary rather than something to settle here.

Whichever way it goes, this file needs to stop naming `hourly` before missingbulb/Claudinite#1234 can merge its frequency half.
